key_insight: MambaVF reformulates video fusion as a sequential state-update process using state space models (SSMs), enabling temporal fusion without explicit optical flow or feature warping. This approach yields much lower computational overhead and better scalability for multi-frame fusion.
problem_solved: Existing video fusion methods depend on costly optical flow estimation and feature warping, which limits runtime efficiency and scalability to long sequences or high-resolution video. MambaVF removes that bottleneck by performing temporal modeling through SSMs.
method: Recast video fusion as a sequential state update problem where a learned SSM evolves a compact state carrying temporal information across frames.
Use the SSM to aggregate temporal context and produce fused frame representations directly, eliminating optical-flow-based motion estimation and explicit warping.
Train the pipeline end-to-end to decode fused outputs from the evolving state, focusing on compute- and parameter-efficient SSM modules for real-time-friendly inference.
impact: For practitioners, MambaVF offers a path to faster, more scalable video fusion pipelines that reduce runtime and memory cost while retaining temporal coherence — enabling deployment on resource-constrained hardware and longer sequences.
